title: PR contract & refactor scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for PR review heuristics, contract checks, refactor follow-ups, and things I keep forgetting in big diffs. Not for sharing yet — raw notes.

High-level goals:
- Keep PRs focused on a single intent (behavioral change OR mechanical refactor, rarely both).
- Guard API contracts and public model inputs/outputs.
- Surface perf/alloc regressions early with quick local checks.
- Leave clear, small follow-ups rather than one huge follow-up task.

Checklist (quick run for every PR > 4 files or touching public surface):
1) Title & description clarity: what changed, why, migration steps, rollback plan. Example: "shard-routing: prefer local cache then fallback to remote; migration: noop"
2) API surface: public functions, proto messages, HTTP routes — list them and check compatibility. If breaking change, add migration doc + deprecation header.
3) Feature flags: is the change behind a flag? If not, justify. Add a canary rollout plan (percent windows, metric burn-in).
4) Observability: add metrics/tracing for new control paths (counter + latency histogram + error tag). New metric names: prefixed with service name, e.g., serving.runtime.prefix_request_cache_hit.
5) Tests: unit + integration paths. If touching cache/kv: add a perf-smoke that runs 5k seq-length-16 tokens on dev GPU.
6) Benchmarks: include before/after (p50/p95/p99 and memory). If none, add TODO to run nightly microbenchmark job (add ticket).
7) Linting & formatting: ensure formatter and proto lints pass. If renaming a proto field, update docs and client stubs.
8) Security: any data plane changes? audit for sensitive fields and KMS usage.
9) Docs: include short user-facing blurb for Console and API changelog.
10) Rollback: clear steps (revert PR + database/flag changes) and known side effects.

PR size heuristics (personal):
- <= 10 files, <= 300 lines: easy review window.
- 10-25 files or >300 lines: needs walkthrough + at least two reviewers.
- >25 files or cross-service: break into multiple PRs or write a 2–3 paragraph explainer and schedule 30-min review sync.

Refactor notes (common pain points):
- "Extract function" drift: watch for behavior changes when extracting code that relied on local mutation/state. Add explicit parameters instead of closed-over vars.
- Proto changes: avoid renaming in place — prefer additive fields + deprecate. If renaming unavoidable, provide conversion layer.
- Centralized config: when moving config keys across layers, leave adapters for one release to avoid split-brain.
- Thread safety: double-check use of cached singletons and lazy statics in multi-threaded runtime.

Performance quick-check recipe (local):
- Run unit perf harness with same model/seq_length combo used in QA. Script: tools/bench/run_local.sh --model=x --seq=32 --iters=200.
- Compare p50/p95/p99 against baseline in /bench/baselines/{model}.json. If regression > 10% p95, block unless documented.
- Heap snapshot: run python tracemalloc (or relevant tool) for token-forward path. High alloc at request edge -> consider streaming/prefix-cache.

Observability & tagging conventions I keep forgetting:
- metric names: service.component.operation.unit (serving.runtime.decode.lat_ms).
- tracing: use span tags "model.name", "model.revision", "route.id".
- logs: structured JSON; error logs must include request_id & route.

Follow-ups (small tickets preferred):
- F1: Add a presubmit check that fails if PR touches both "/internal/" and "/public/" without updated changelog (ticket INF-1203).
- F2: Script to auto-generate stub for proto field deprecation warnings in client SDKs.
- F3: Nightly perf job to capture small-model (seq=16) and large-model (seq=1024) baselines for any PR touching serving runtime.
- F4: Add template snippet in PR description for rollout plan and metrics to watch.

Notes-to-self (throwaway):
- When approving refactors, ask for a one-line footnote in PR: "no behavior change; verified by unit/integ with flag=on/off". Saves future confusion.
- If a PR touches model routing and cache, prefer canary in one region for 24-48h before full rollout.
- For HTTP contract changes, check SDK generator output locally (tools/sdk-gen/).

Examples (quick snippets to paste in review comments):
- "Can you add a unit test that simulates a cache TTL expiration path? I've seen bugs when TTL boundary hits and we fall through to remote incorrectly."
- "Why is this mutex covering IO? Consider narrower lock (protect only metadata) and use concurrent IO path."
- "Please add a metric for 'fallback_to_remote' with tags (route, reason) so we can triage frequency by route."

Open questions / unresolved:
- How aggressive should we be with proto additive-only policy vs. developer speed for small internal protos? Tradeoff table needed.
- Is there a low-effort way to detect behavioral refactors vs. mechanical? Maybe by running recorded request diff harness (record replay) in CI.

Tiny checklist to leave in PR comments (copy/paste):
- [ ] Description: intent, migration, rollback
- [ ] Feature flag/canary plan
- [ ] Metrics/tracing added
- [ ] Tests added/updated
- [ ] Perf baseline attached or ticketed
- [ ] Docs updated (API + Console blurb)

Brain dump end. Save and revisit next time I review cross-service PRs — try to force more small follow-ups, fewer giant todos.

Misc links I keep opening:
- Confluence: /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=API-CONTRACTS
- Repo perf job: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/workflows/bench.yml
- Proto lint: tools/protolint/config.yaml

---
Tiny personal footer:
If in doubt, call the author for a 10-min walkthrough. Saves 2 hrs of comment ping-pong.
